cases.name: The Infinity Smuggler
cases.cause: Python's JSON parser can turn a large numeric token into Infinity without calling parse_constant.
cases.finding: A bounded Python fixture checks the overflow, the missing parse_constant callback and finite-number countermeasures.
cases.mitigation: Use finite-validating parse_float or Decimal for suitable workloads; serialize with allow_nan=False.
cases.scope: Python 3 JSON behaviour on the tested runtime. Does not prove application-specific numeric constraints.

cases.name: The Stdin Custody Battle
cases.teaser: Two inputs entered. One descriptor left.
cases.cause: A shell heredoc consumes stdin assigned to Python source, displacing a piped data stream.
cases.finding: Linux/Bash subprocess fixture demonstrates the descriptor collision and working alternative; SIGPIPE only labelled observed when exit status confirms it.
cases.mitigation: Use python3 -c or another source-loading method that leaves stdin for incoming pipe data.
cases.scope: Linux, Bash and Python 3; upstream SIGPIPE timing may vary.

cases.name: Schrödinger’s Backup
cases.teaser: Integrity check: OK. Missing row: also OK?
cases.cause: Copying only SQLite's main database file can omit committed data still present in its WAL.
cases.finding: Disposable SQLite WAL fixture compares raw file copy against SQLite's backup API and records both row visibility and integrity checks.
cases.mitigation: Use SQLite-aware backup mechanisms instead of copying only a live main database file.
cases.scope: Controlled SQLite WAL and checkpoint state, not all backups or workloads.

cases.name: The CRCRLF Tribunal
cases.cause: Naively converting every LF to CRLF duplicates CR bytes in already-CRLF input.
cases.finding: Linux byte-level fixture records CRCRLF output and an idempotent normalization control.
cases.mitigation: Normalize CRLF and lone CR to LF first, then convert to the desired newline convention.
cases.scope: Byte transformation reproduced on Linux. Windows cmd.exe parsing was NOT tested.

cases.name: The CUDA Apparition
cases.teaser: The GPU has declined to testify.
cases.cause: CUDA assertion behaviour is a proposed investigation, not an established finding.
cases.finding: Placeholder manifest only; no executed reproducer or receipt is claimed.
cases.mitigation: Define a safe GPU fixture and collect genuine hardware-specific evidence before promotion.
cases.scope: NOT TESTED. No GPU results or platform claims.

cases.name: The Louvain Shape-Shifter
cases.cause: Proposed instability investigation awaiting a bounded fixture and verified observations.
cases.finding: Placeholder only; no executed reproduction or receipt is claimed.
cases.mitigation: Pin graph/data and library versions, control seeds, and define measurable graph outcomes.

cases.name: The Ancestor That Refused to Die
cases.formal: The Ancestor That Refused to Die
cases.teaser: The common ancestor kept showing up.
cases.cause: A three-marker merge parser can mistake Git diff3's extra ancestor block for ours.
cases.finding: A disposable real Git merge produced the diff3 markers; naive and corrected parsers were compared.
cases.mitigation: Handle all four diff3 markers, validate order, and limit any automatic conflict resolution.
cases.scope: One bounded non-nested conflict pattern; not a universal Git conflict resolver.

cases.name: The Git Identity Crisis
cases.teaser: git -C pointed here. GIT_DIR pointed elsewhere.
cases.cause: GIT_DIR overrides repository discovery even when git -C selects another working directory.
cases.finding: Two disposable Git repositories show a successful add to the wrong index while the intended index stays unchanged.
cases.mitigation: Keep reserved Git environment variables unset unless intended; inspect --absolute-git-dir before mutations.
cases.scope: Executed with Git CLI on Linux; original Windows batch script NOT tested.

cases.name: The Double-Delivery Department
cases.cause: Two read-first SQLite queue drainers can claim the same pending message.
cases.finding: Deterministic SQLite WAL interleavings show double delivery, busy-snapshot upgrade and conditional claiming under BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
cases.mitigation: Use atomic conditional claims, short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions and idempotent processing.
cases.scope: Single-process deterministic interleaving. Does not promise external exactly-once delivery.

cases.name: The Emoji That Broke the Signature
cases.formal: The Emoji That Broke the Signature
cases.teaser: Two alphabets disagreed about the queue.
cases.cause: Python's code-point key sorting differs from JCS UTF-16 ordering for certain supplementary and BMP keys.
cases.finding: Independent byte-order fixture compares serialized output and SHA-256 digests under each ordering.
cases.mitigation: Implement full JCS with UTF-16 key ordering and all required numeric/escaping rules.
cases.scope: Key-order subset only; not a complete JCS or live JavaScript interoperability test.

cases.name: The Anchor That Became a FIFO
cases.formal: The Anchor That Became a FIFO
cases.teaser: The pathname had an alibi. The descriptor had the evidence.
cases.cause: A separate pathname check and open can see different objects; hardcoding x86-64 O_NOFOLLOW on ARM64 silently weakens symlink protection.
cases.finding: Isolated Python syscall-pattern reproductions passed on Linux x86-64 and ARM64. TOMBSTONE Rust's separate eight-configuration CI passed. The two are distinct evidence scopes.
cases.mitigation: Open with native no-follow/nonblocking flags; fstat and bounded-read the SAME descriptor; retain an independent trust anchor.
cases.scope: Linux x86-64 and ARM64; not all kernels, hardware, historical custody or Rust execution by the Python fixture.
